Titherley and G. Basford were second and third in the local 220yds race.
Ring won the Walk, and G. Basford was second in the 100yds. at Luton.
At our evening meeting on May 20th, eight Club handicaps were held, and a noticeable feature was the double successes of three members, G.
Morgan won both the 100 yards and 200 yards handicaps confined to Police held at this meeting. At Belvedere, G. Basford was second in both sprints, and C.
Odell won the 100 yards for us, with G.
Green as second, Farrington third; and our 220 yards champion, George Basford, fourth. Victory in the Walk went to the youngest competitor, L.
George Basford, our 220 yards Champion, running over an unaccustomed distance, did well to hand over with the bunch, and Michael, running a well-judged quarter, took us into third position.
In the 100 yards we had first and second with Hugh Dulson and George Basford. We also annexed the first two places in the 220 yards with Ernie Jarvis and Jock Wilcock.

George Basford ran next and maintained this lead; Stroud on the next 220 had Pallett as his opponent and as they had to cross at the finish in order to reach their waiting club-mates, (Herne Hill were drawn No. 1 with ourselves No. 4), the Herne Hill half-miler Thorpe went off about a yard in front of Tommy Scrimshaw.
Stroud did the first double of the day by winning this race in addition to the hundred. A past holder, G.

We were very pleased to see our old sprinter George Basford at some of our last season's meetings and hope that other old-time members will do their best to come along and see what talent there is at present wearing the "claret and gold" and am sure they will not be disappointed.
